name: Legislative/Lobby Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Legislative / Lobby Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Monday, August 12, 2024
  2:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  August 12, 2024 / 2:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember John Mirisch, Deputy City
  Manager Keith Sterling, Municipal Affairs Program Manager Cynthia
  Owens, Chief of Police Mark Stainbrook, Fire Chief Gregory Barton,
  Director of Public Works Shana Epstein

  A. Oral Communications:
  a. The office of Rick Chavez Zbur sent a representative who requested that he
  present his public comment during agenda item B-8, which was approved by the
  Liaisons.

  B. Direction:
  1. H.R. - Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act
  i. This bill is opposed by the Biden administration, numerous law
  enforcement agencies, and District Attorneys.
  ii. The Chief of Police Mark Stainbrook also opposes the bill.
  iii. Both Liaisons oppose the bill.
  2. California Proposition 36, Drug and Theft Crime Penalties and Treatment-
  Mandated Felonies Initiative (2024)
  i. Both Liaisons support the proposition.
  3. City of Glendora’s League of California Cities Resolution
  i. Both Liaisons support the resolution.
  ii. Neither of the Liaisons will be able to make it to the League of California
  Cities conference to formally endorse the resolution. The city will be
  sending Keith Sterling as their representative to the conference.
  4. Senate Bill 226 (Alvarado-Gil) - Controlled Substances: armed possession:
  fentanyl.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  5. Assembly Bill 2081 (Davies) - Substance abuse: recovery and treatment programs.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  6. Assembly Bill 2574 (Valencia) - Alcoholism or drug abuse recovery or treatment
  program and facilities: disclosures.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  7. Assembly Bill 3218 (Wood) - Unflavored Tobacco List.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  8. Assembly Bill 2498 (Zbur) - Housing: the California Housing Security Act.
 Highlights for August 12 2024
Legislative / Lobby Committee

  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  ii. The office of Rick Chavez Zbur sent a representative to request for the
  City’s support for AB 2498 and also informed the Liaisons that AB 2943
  had passed the legislature and thanked the Liaisons for their support of the
  bill
  9. Assembly Bill 3093 (Ward) - Land use: housing element: streamlined multifamily
  housing.
  i. Both Liaisons oppose the bill unless it is amended to satisfy the League of
  California Cities’ concerns.
  10. Senate Bill 610 (Wiener) - Fire Prevention: Wildfire mitigation area: defensible
  space: State Fire Marshal.
  i. The Chief of the Fire Department Gregory Barton believes that the bill
  needs to be significantly amended before he can support it.
  ii. Both Liaisons oppose the bill.
  11. Assembly Bill: 2557 (Ortega) - Local agencies: contracts for special services and
  temporary help: performance report.
  i. Both Liaisons oppose the bill.
  12. Assembly Bill 2561 (McKinnor) - Local public employees: vacant positions.
  i. Both Liaisons oppose the bill.
  13. Assembly Bill 1890 (Patterson, Joe) - Public works: prevailing wage.
  i. Both Liaisons oppose the bill.
  14. Assembly Bill 2286 (Aguiar-Curry) - Vehicles: autonomous vehicles.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  15. Assembly Bill 3179 (Carrilo, Juan) – Emergency telecommunications medium- and
  heavy-duty zero-emission vehicles.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  16. Senate Bill 1255 (Durazo) - Public water systems: needs analysis: water rate
  assistance program
  i. The Director of Public Works Shana Epstein is opposed to the bill.
  ii. Both Liaisons oppose the bill.
  17. Assembly Bill 2631 (Fong, Mike) - Local agencies: ethics training.
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  18. H.R. 3565 the Spectrum Auction Reauthorization Act of 2023
  i. Both Liaisons support the bill.
  19. Legislative Updates
  i. Congress needs to pass a stopgap funding bill before the end of September
  in order to prevent a government shutdown.
  ii. The Senate overwhelmingly passed the Kids Online Safety Act and the
  Children and Teens Online Privacy Protection Act which aim to protect
  children’s privacy online. These bills are expected to be heard in the house
  before the end of the year.
  iii. The California legislature has until August 31st to pass all legislation from
  the current session.
  iv. Governor Newsom has announced the selection of Ian Choudri as the new
  Chief Executive Officer for the California High Speed Rail Authority pending
  the approval of the CAHSR governing board.
  v. The governor also issues an executive order directing state agencies to
  clean up homeless encampments on state owned property.
  vi. The State announced that 27.5% of all new vehicle purchases in California
  were EVs.
 Highlights for August 12 2024
Legislative / Lobby Committee

  vii. The state received $600 million in federal grants to upgrade 100 miles of
  electric transmission lines with grid enhancing technologies to improve grid
  reliability.
  viii. The Governor also announced an award of $94 million for infill housing
  projects.
  ix. State Senator Alvarado-Gil has announced he is switching from the
  Democratic to the Republican party.
  x. The governor has also issued an executive order to direct the California
  Department of Insurance to try and stabilize the insurance market. Vice
  Mayor Nazarian would like a presentation on this executive order to be
  added as an informational item to a future Council Agenda.
  20. Future Agenda Items Discussion
  i. Councilmember Mirisch would like to discuss LA County Measure A
  ii. He also wishes to discuss a proposal to increase the number of LA County
  supervisors from 5 to 9 which he believes the city should support.

  C. Adjournment:
  Date / Time: August 12, 2024 / 2:51 PM
